title: robots.txt route disappears when the frontend build is absent
reasoning: GET /robots.txt is only registered inside the frontend-build conditional. In environments where the backend runs without a copied frontend index, the route is not present at all, so clients get the default 404 instead of a stable robots.txt response. That makes the advertised route depend on an unrelated SPA artifact rather than the robots.txt contract itself.
reproduction: Run the FastAPI app from a checkout where frontend/index.html is absent, then request GET /robots.txt; the robots handler is never registered.
recommendation: Register /robots.txt unconditionally, or at least independently check for and serve an available robots.txt with a safe fallback response such as a small text/plain policy or an explicit 404.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover GET /robots.txt or app startup without the frontend build artifact.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a TestClient test that imports the app with no frontend/index.html present and asserts GET /robots.txt returns the intended stable status/body rather than depending on the SPA build gate.
minimumFixScope: Adjust the /robots.txt route registration in app/main.py and add a focused route test.
